subject: Reserved commit + burst add-on — proposed credit-slab addendum
messages:
From: Samir Desai <s.desai@aureliahealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool sizing + burst cost questions

Neha — thanks for the walkthrough earlier. A couple of items came up internally that I wanted on the record before we get to legal:

1) Peak hours: our nightly batch + daytime traffic creates two clear peaks. We need an upper bound on burst costs for budgeting — spikes of up to 6x baseline in 2–3 hour windows. Can you provide a predictable way to cap or smooth the surge billing?

2) Cooldown behavior: if we spike today, how is that amortized across the month? Is it "used then billed" or can it be credit-slabbed/averaged so our finance team doesn't see massive one-off charges?

3) Throughput guarantee: what are you willing to commit on p95 generation latency for 2k context with our preferred model family? We need something we can put in our SOW.

Appreciate concrete numbers so I can move this to procurement/IT.

— Samir
Procurement, Aurelia Health
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Samir Desai <s.desai@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>; Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T11:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Reserved commit + burst add-on — proposed credit-slab addendum

Samir — thanks for the clear list. Summarizing our proposal below so procurement has one doc to review (attached is a formal addendum PDF and the sizing sheet). High level: our aim is to keep baseline economics predictable while giving you a bounded and lower-cost way to handle the spikes you described.

Proposal (baseline + burst credit-slab):
- Baseline reserved commit: 4 A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved capacity, monthly commit) — $58,000 / month. Includes dedicated pool, isolation, and throughput optimization.
- Throughput guarantee: p95 token generation latency <= 350ms at 2,048 context for model family indicated in the sizing sheet. SLA credits for missed p95 commitments (detailed in addendum).
- Burst capacity: credit-slab model rather than per-hour surge pricing. You purchase a monthly burst credit bucket in tiers:
  * Tier A — 10 GPU-hours of surge credit at 0.6x baseline rate (meant for ad-hoc small spikes)
  * Tier B — 50 GPU-hours at 0.9x baseline rate
  * Tier C — 200 GPU-hours at 1.25x baseline rate (for sustained multi-hour peaks)
- Credit consumption mechanism: credits are deducted from the slab with priority from Tier A -> B -> C. If you exceed all slabs, excess uses emergency surge rate (1.9x) but only after we provide a 24-hour advance notification option (customer can opt out of emergency surge).
- Cooldown and reconciliation: instead of a hard cooldown window, we propose a 30-day rolling reconciliation. Spikes are amortized over the 30-day window using a decaying credit curve so a single short spike doesn't blow the monthly invoice. This is what your finance team asked for; we can show example amortization in the spreadsheet.
- Commit smoothing: reserved commit can be shared across two logical teams under Aurelia (if you want to split between Clinical and Ops) with a single pooled billing view.

Next steps:
1) If this structure looks acceptable, Marissa will confirm discount bands and Lauren will confirm billing/legal language for the addendum.
2) We'll produce an SOW + DocuSign link for signature (I attached v3 of the addendum with placeholders).

Open to a quick sync — I can join your procurement call tomorrow if helpful.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T13:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Reserved commit + burst add-on — proposed credit-slab addendum

Neha / Lauren — quick internal notes on the pricing bands after reviewing the sizing sheet:

- Discounting: we can offer a volume discount on the baseline commit if Aurelia moves to a 12-month prepay (up to 8% off listed baseline) or a 24-month commit (up to 12%). I suggest we reserve 6% in the quote for now and surface the 12% as a close incentive.
- Tier pricing rationale: Tier C at 1.25x is intentionally below the emergency surge so it remains attractive for heavy but planned peaks; the emergency surge (1.9x) remains our backstop. This should be acceptable for a hospital where predictability matters.
- Cooldown wording: legal will want to avoid open-ended credits. We need to convert "rolling reconciliation" into a clear algorithm in the addendum (decay rate, lookback window). I can coordinate with legal to insert a formula-based clause.
- Attachments: I'll add a sample month-level amortization example. Also recommend we include an opt-in clause for advances notice to limit emergency surge usage.

If you want, I can draft the specific discount clause and the amortization table this afternoon. Happy to hop on a 30-min call.

— Marissa
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Samir Desai <s.desai@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>; Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-06T17:23:00-08:00
Subject: Final draft addendum + signature link (includes amortization examples)

Samir — attaching the v3 addendum and the example amortization sheet. We've incorporated Marissa's discount guidance and formalized the 30-day rolling amortization algorithm (decay factor = 0.5 per 7-day period) in section 2.3 of the addendum. Key updates since my last note: 

- Baseline reserved commit remains 4 GPUs at $58,000/mo (6% discount applied if you sign a 12-month prepay; 12% if 24-month prepay).
- Burst slabs unchanged; added a hard cap opt-in: if you check the "monthly spend cap" box, we will throttle burst to avoid exceeding the cap and send an invoice for any throttled capacity at the next review.
- SLA: p95 <= 350ms at 2,048 tokens; formal SLA credits described in Sec 4.
- Billing: monthly invoice with line items for baseline, burst credit usage (consumption and spent slab), and any emergency surge. Amortized spike effect will be visible as a separate "reconciliation" line showing spread across 30 days.

DocuSign: https://docusign.example/link/AX7B3F-2026
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example/deal/78431

If Aurelia confirms the cap behavior and the 12-month prepay discount, legal can route a final SOW. Let me know if you want one more worked example for your CFO; Marissa included a sample month in the spreadsheet.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
